conviction_note: The quarter is almost entirely pre-released: UP, about 87% of UIE's asset value, published its record Q3 on 11 Nov, Schörling's value can be worked out from listed share prices, and the FY2026 outlook ('lower net profit than 2025', USD 139.9m) is near-certain to be repeated. So the move is sized as a pre-released print on a low-volatility holding company (2.2%) with a coin-flip sign tilted slightly up (p_up 53), because UIE has closed flat-to-up on 7 of its last 8 own release days and the buyback bids every day; the findings sum (+0.2) and the scaled number (+0.13) agree and are both near zero.

already_public.what: United Plantations (48.4% owned, ~87% of UIE asset value) Q3 2026 net profit RM290.93m vs RM203.28m (+43.1%); 9M RM645.58m (+4.8%); interim 30 sen + special 15 sen dividend payable 8 Dec 2026
Same UP Q3 2026 print, revenue RM722.22m, prices resilient, refinery contribution
UIE FY2026 outlook: 'UIE is currently projecting a lower net profit for the year compared to 2025' (FY2025 = USD 139.9m); H1 2026 net result USD 10.5m; Schörling fair value -USD 12.4m YTD at 18 Aug

Schörling's listed holdings Q3 2026 (30 Jun -> 30 Sep): Hexagon +23.0% (~40% of Schörling NAV), Hexpol +33.6%, AAK -19.4%, ASSA ABLOY +3.9%, Securitas -3.1%, Beijer Ref +5.1%; SEK -3.0% vs USD; all public prices
Weekly buyback disclosures: 219,428 shares / DKK 88.2m of the DKK 150m programme bought by 13 Nov, 4,000 shares a day

new_in_release.expect: Q3 net result of roughly USD 40-50m (UP share ~USD 34.5m = RM290.93m x 48.4% x 0.245 USD/MYR, plus a positive Schörling fair-value change), similar to Q3 2025's ~USD 45.2m. 9M of roughly USD 55m against USD 106.8m. All of it can be worked out from public data, so no surprise in either direction.

The 'lower net profit than 2025' wording is most likely repeated. 9M ~USD 55m against a FY2025 of USD 139.9m makes an upgrade arithmetically implausible. The YTD Schörling fair-value figure quoted in the outlook should be less negative than -12.4m, a mild positive in tone only.
The Greenbridge (unlisted software) fair-value change is unknown and is ~3% of assets. It is the only genuinely unseen number, and too small to matter.
None expected. UIE pays annually, after the AGM.

bar: unsourced: no sell-side consensus (Yahoo returns no quarters, analyst_count null). The effective bar is the arithmetic from UP's published Q3 and public share prices, so every size is capped small.
session_check: bmo (window-equivalent). The issuer's financial calendar lists '17 November 2026 Third Quarter Report 2026' with no time (https://www.uie.dk/financial-calendar). Past release times from the Nasdaq feed: Q3 2025 at 08:32 CET, before the 09:00 open; H1 2026 at 09:59 CEST, Q1 2026 at 11:22 CEST and Q3 2024 at 13:39 CET, all in session. Every one of these falls inside the close(16 Nov) -> close(17 Nov) window, so the bmo window is correct whether the release comes before the open or during the session; it is not amc. UP has already reported (11 Nov), so UIE's release no longer waits on UP's board meeting.
positioning_check: No disclosed net short position. UIE is absent from Finanstilsynet's aggregated net short register as of 30-10-2026, which publishes from 0.1%, so this is a near-true zero rather than a 0.5% truncation (https://www.dfsa.dk/financial-themes/capital-market/company-announcements/aggregated-net-short-positions). No change can be computed. The only visible systematic flow is the company's own Safe Harbour buyback via DNB Carnegie at 4,000 shares a day, about a quarter of normal daily volume.

findings.finding: UP's Q3 2026 net profit of RM290.93m (+43.1% y/y) was published on 11 Nov, so UIE's share of UP for Q3 (~USD 34.5m against ~USD 23.4m in Q3 2025) is already public. UIE rose from DKK 388.0 (10 Nov close) to 399.5-403 since.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UIE's own release-day closes (Yahoo tape): Q3 2025 +1.7%, H1 2025 +1.9%, Q1 2025 +2.2%, FY2024 -2.9%, FY2025 +0.3%, Q1 2026 +0.1%, H1 2026 +2.5%. UP's own Q3 day moved UIE +1.0% on 11 Nov and +1.0% on 12 Nov 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: UIE climbed ~3% in the four sessions after UP's print on rising volume (15k -> 55k shares). The only unpriced part is Danish retail reading the headline in UIE's own USD release, which has historically coincided with flat-to-up release days. If it were not priced, UIE would still sit at DKK 388.

findings.finding: Schörling's listed holdings rose through Q3 (Hexagon +23.0%, about 40% of its NAV; Hexpol +33.6%; partly offset by AAK -19.4%; SEK -3.0% vs USD). UIE's Q3 fair-value line on Schörling (USD 215.4m at 30 Jun) should therefore be positive, roughly USD +10-15m, after USD -32.0m in H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The H1 2026 report carried a USD -32.0m Schörling fair-value loss and the stock rose +2.5% on the day. Q1 2026 carried -36.3m and it moved +0.1%. The line has not decided the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is computable from public prices, and Schörling is only ~8% of UIE's assets, so it is priced. It is filed because it flips the headline net result versus H1 and the YTD Schörling figure in the outlook paragraph, which is where a retail reader may notice it. The weights for holdings other than Hexagon are not disclosed per holding in the report, so this is an inference.
findings.independence: https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a3faa4d569e49edada9cb18f437cf66c7 (H1 2026 report: Hexagon ~40% of Schörling NAV, USD 215.4m fair value at 30 Jun)

findings.finding: The FY2026 outlook in force says UIE is projecting a lower net profit than 2025's USD 139.9m. With H1 at USD 10.5m and Q3 at roughly USD 45m, the Q3 report will almost surely repeat it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 report ('materially higher net profit in 2025') +1.7%; H1 2026 report introducing 'lower net profit' +2.5%. The guide has been mechanical and has not moved the stock against its direction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It is filed at 0 because an unchanged guide is the expected outcome; a wording change toward 'on level with 2025' would be a genuine surprise and is arithmetically implausible.

findings.finding: UIE's Safe Harbour buyback keeps buying 4,000 shares every session (DKK 88.2m of DKK 150m spent by 13 Nov, average DKK 402.08), a steady bid of roughly a quarter of normal daily volume through the release day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Weekly disclosures since 20 Aug 2026 have not moved the stock; it has ranged DKK 387.5-403 through Oct-Nov.
findings.original_quote: UIE'S SHARE BUY-BACK PROGRAMME ... Accumulated under the programme 219,428 ... 402.08 ... 88,228,548 (the Danish version is headed 'UIEs aktietilbagekøbsprogram')
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed every week and fully priced. It dampens a downside reaction on the day rather than adding upside, which is why it is filed at 0 with an upside-skewed range.

findings.finding: UP warned that the continued freeze on guest-worker recruitment 'will present serious challenges as the industry approaches its next production peak in March/April 2027'. UIE's Q3 outlook paragraph will probably repeat this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior case of this line on UIE.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 11 Nov and the stock rose afterwards, so it is priced. It concerns 2027 production, beyond anything this window settles.

outside_window.finding: UP's interim 30 sen + special 15 sen dividend, payable 8 Dec 2026, lifts UIE's cash by roughly RM135m (~USD 33m) in Q4

baseline_tension: The evidence is neutral-to-mildly positive and agrees with the +2.9% 20-day and +3.2% 5-day run-up (which already captured UP's print) rather than with the small negative run-up lean (-0.147). There is no short register position to fight.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. UIE publishes its reports in English only and its regulatory notices in both languages (e.g. 'Igangsættelse af nyt aktietilbagekøbsprogram' alongside 'Initiation of a new share buy-back programme'). Danish-language search returned only aggregator pages and an August Økonomisk Ugebrev NAV-discount note already in the H1 report. The decisive information this quarter is Malaysian (UP's Bursa print, reported by NST/The Star in English).
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the UP Q3 finding went from +0.3 to +0.1 and the Schörling inference from +0.2 to +0.1 (both public); the buyback (+0.1) and labour-warning (-0.1) findings went to 0.0.

'Size the move on what is new; let reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': abs_move_pct went from 1.8 (the name's own release-day median) to 2.2, toward the 3% pre-released base, and is held below 3% only because this is a 15%-vol holding company whose period is fully computable. p_up went from 54 to 53, inside the 45-55 band for a pre-released period with an unchanged guide.
